To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate constant for SET from tributyl phosphine to methyl- or ethyl-substituted viologen in acetonitritrile–methaol is 10–100 times faster when the viologen has a deuterium atom at the 4 position than when it has a proton at this position.
the rate of single electron transfer from tributyl-phosphine to methyl-substituted viologens is significantly affected by deuterium substitution at the methyl carbon atom.

the rate constant for single-electron transfer occurring between tributylphos-phine and a viologen depends on the isotopic composition of the viologen methyl substituent, and the kinetic deuterium effect is consistent with SET occurring within a solvent-separated ion pair formed between the two reactants.
